name: Sensory Evaluation of Food

objectives.text: Describe a food using the senses of taste, smell, sight, touch, and hearing
Identify the five basic tastes of sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami in common food samples
Compare two food samples using taste, texture, aroma, and appearance
Explain how the sense of smell combines with taste to create the flavor of a food
Explain why different people perceive the same food differently because of factors such as age, genetics, and cultural background
Use precise sensory vocabulary to describe the texture, aroma, and flavor attributes of a food sample
Demonstrate proper blind taste test technique including coded samples, randomized serving order, and palate cleansing between samples
Record sensory judgments of food samples using a hedonic rating scale
Explain how sources of bias such as color expectations, brand labels, sample order, and taster fatigue can distort sensory results
Distinguish between affective consumer tests and analytical tests such as discrimination and descriptive tests by purpose and design
Conduct a triangle or duo-trio difference test to determine whether two food samples are perceptibly different
Interpret sensory panel data to determine consumer preference and market potential among food samples
Explain how food processors use sensory evaluation in quality assurance to detect off-flavors, defects, and inconsistencies
Evaluate dairy, meat, and produce samples against industry sensory quality criteria as used in FFA Food Science and Milk Quality career development events
Analyze how food constituents such as fat, sugar, salt, and moisture influence the sensory qualities of a food product
Apply statistical tables or basic significance testing to determine whether sensory test results reflect real differences between samples
Select and train sensory panelists by screening for taste acuity and calibrating them to reference standards
Evaluate the reliability of a sensory evaluation method based on panel size, panelist training, replication, and control of bias
Design a sensory evaluation protocol to test consumer acceptance of a newly developed food product for an SAE or FFA project
Recommend product reformulation or corrective quality procedures based on sensory evaluation findings

changes: Kept all six existing objectives as real competencies, rewording a few: added hearing to the grade 3 senses, added coding, randomization, and palate cleansing to the grade 7 blind test, and broadened the grade 9 data interpretation to include market potential and moved it to grade 10. Added the five basic tastes, smell's role in flavor, individual differences in perception, sensory vocabulary, hedonic scales, and sources of bias for the elementary and middle grades. Added the high school sequence: affective versus analytical tests, difference testing, quality assurance use, CDE-style product evaluation, how constituents shape sensory qualities, statistical significance, panelist screening and training, and reformulation recommendations. The design objective now ties to SAE and FFA work. Standards are mapped only to grade 9 to 12 objectives they directly teach.
